Article Title: As companies in America face rising health costs, Starbucks ends employee benefits' coverage for these medicines
Article Text:
Reason behind Starbucks pulling back coverage for weight-loss drugs

Starbucks discontinued its AI inventory tool

Starbucks has announced that it will stop covering the GLP-1 medications prescribed for weight loss under its employee health plans starting October. According to a report by Business Insider, the Seattle-based coffee chain has confirmed that while the drugs may still be covered for other conditions such as diabetes, they will no longer be included for weight-loss purposes. Starbucks provides health benefits to full- and part-time employees working at least 20 hours a week.This move by Starbucks reflects a broader trend among US employers recalibrating benefits as spending on GLP-1 drugs surges. Originally developed for diabetes, these medicines have become popular for obesity treatment. According to the International Foundation of Employee Benefit Plans, GLP-1 drugs accounted for 11.4% of corporate employers’ total annual claims in 2025, up from 6.9% in 2023. Average health-benefit costs per employee rose 6% last year and are projected to climb another 6.7% this year, with GLP-1 usage cited as a major driver.Other large employers have also pulled back coverage. As per the Business Insider report, Allina Health ended GLP-1 coverage for weight loss in January 2025, citing rising premiums, while PwC has reportedly made similar changes. At the same time, some companies are doubling down: Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan recently said the bank spends more than $250 million annually on GLP-1 coverage, viewing it as an investment in employee health.In related news, in May this year, Starbucks announced that it is discontinuing its AI-powered inventory management tool. According to a Fortune report, the company decided to stop using the system after employees raised concerns about its accuracy. The tool, developed by NomadGo, was introduced in September last year to automatically count inventory items such as milk and syrups and help stores manage stock levels. However, workers said the app often made mistakes, leading to operational problems. According to Carl Addison, a Starbucks shift supervisor in Washington state, the system required stores to reorganise storage areas, adding extra work for employees. “The app’s inaccuracies made employees’ workflow more challenging,” Addison told Fortune.
Article Summary: Starbucks will stop covering the GLP-1 medications prescribed for weight loss under its employee health plans starting October. The drugs may still be covered for other conditions such as diabetes, but they will no longer be included for weight-loss purposes. Starbucks provides health benefits to full- and part-time employees working at least 20 hours a week. This move by Starbucks reflects a broader trend among US employers recalibrating benefits.

Article Title: Scientists turn Sharks into real-time ocean observers, carrying sensors that can measure conditions for oceanographic, atmospheric and climate models
Article Text:
AI generated image

Researchers decode ocean heat that fuels hurricanes

Tagging executed like a ‘Pit Crew’

Researchers from University of Delaware are transforming how oceanographers (scientists who study the earth's oceans) track marine conditions by deploying specialised electronic tags that turn living sharks into mobile, real-time data collection hubs. The research project, led by marine scientist Aaron Carlisle, equips predatory fish with advanced sensors designed to collect water profiles across the US East Coast.Instead of merely tracking animal movements, the tags gather critical data on temperature, salinity and depth – feeding real-time information directly into atmospheric and climate forecast models. The research was published in journal Frontiers in Conservation Science.The primary goal of the tagging initiative is to map the upper layer of the ocean, known to oceanographers as the mixed layer. This upper column of water holds the thermal energy that directly feeds and amplifies hurricane strength.“This is the part of the water column that really drives hurricane intensity — warmer mixed layer equals stronger hurricane — as it holds the heat that feeds hurricanes,” explained Carlisle, a professor in the university's School of Marine Science and Policy.While oceanographers have deployed sensor tags on marine mammals like elephant seals in polar regions, sharks present a unique advantage for Atlantic storm tracking. They are abundant, widely distributed, and traverse key coastal corridors where major hurricanes develop and gain strength before making landfall.Researchers target migratory species that surface frequently, such as shortfin mako sharks, blue sharks, smooth hammerheads and juvenile great white sharks. Frequent surfacing is critical because the electronic tags must reach the water's surface to transmit cached environmental data up to orbiting satellite networks.The research team conducts offshore expeditions aboard the university’s research vessel, deploying baited lines 30 to 60 kilometres off the Atlantic coast. When a shark is brought alongside the vessel, the team executes the tagging protocol with extreme precision under strict animal welfare guidelines.“The tagging process itself is operated like a pit crew in an auto race,” Carlisle said, emphasising that the procedure typically takes under five minutes. Each animal undergoes a quick health check before being tagged on its dorsal fin. To protect the sharks long-term, the tags are secured using metallic components designed to naturally corrode and shed after a predetermined period.
Article Summary: Researchers decode ocean heat that fuels hurricanes. Tagging executed like a ‘Pit Crew’ Researchers target migratory species that surface frequently, such as shortfin mako sharks, blue sharks, smooth hammerheads and juvenile great white sharks. Frequent surfacing is critical because the electronic tags must reach the water's surface to transmit cached environmental data.

Article Title: Framework hacked: What was stolen, what wasn't, and what the customers should do now
Article Text:
No card numbers leaked, but Framework customers should brace for convincing phishing emails after a zero-day attack on Metabase.

A third-party breach, but Framework's customers pay for it

If you've bought a Framework laptop, check your inbox. The modular PC maker started emailing its entire customer base late on Thursday, August 6, with the kind of note nobody wants to open. Names, email addresses, phone numbers, home and shipping addresses, and login IPs were all sitting in a database that someone else got into. Payment and order information weren't touched, the company says.The break-in didn't happen at Framework. It happened at Metabase, the business intelligence provider Framework hands its data to. Metabase caught the intrusion on August 3 and says the attacker used a zero-day—an unknown flaw, no patch, no warning—to reach customer databases parked on its cloud, affecting versions 1.58 and above. It has since patched the hole and brought in a third-party forensic firm to map how far the damage runs.Framework moved fast once it was told. It rotated credentials across every database tied to its Metabase instance and confirmed nothing outside Metabase was reached, with no changes to admin access. Spokesperson Eric Schumacher told TechCrunch the breach hit "all customers" without giving a figure; outside estimates put Framework's lifetime sales in the hundreds of thousands.For business buyers, the company is still working out whether company names, billing emails and phone numbers went too.Metabase serves more than 100,000 clients, reportedly including McDonald's, T-Mobile and Hugging Face, so Framework may not be the last name on this list. Its own investigation is still open.This is also Framework's second vendor-shaped problem. In January 2024, accounting firm Keating Consulting leaked customer names and emails. Same story, different supplier.The timing stings. Framework raised prices in January, raised them again in March, then told some Laptop 13 Pro preorder customers they'd get less RAM than advertised, with refunds for anyone unwilling to swallow it. A small firm shipping in batches can't absorb a memory shortage the way Dell or Lenovo can.No card numbers leaked. But a name, address and order relationship is plenty for a convincing phishing email. Treat anything claiming to be Framework support with suspicion for a while.
Article Summary: PC maker Framework says a third-party breached its Metabase database. Names, email addresses, phone numbers, home and shipping addresses, and login IPs were all sitting in a database that someone else got into. Payment and order information weren't touched, the company says.

Article Title: Spotify launches Premium Rewards in India, adds brand offers and invite-only events for subscribers
Article Text:
What's on offer



How subscribers can access it



Spotify has rolled out Premium Rewards in India, a new limited-edition initiative that gives Premium subscribers access to curated brand offers and invite-only live experiences, the company announced on Wednesday. The move adds a lifestyle and events layer on top of the music streaming service's existing offering of high-quality, ad-free, offline listening.Premium Rewards is built around two categories of benefits. The first is lifestyle perks — exclusive offers from partner brands including MakeMyTrip, Tira, Nykaa, Ajio Luxe, Gully Labs and Airbnb, spanning travel, beauty, fashion and lifestyle categories. The second is what Spotify is calling "IRL experiences": invite-only events, intimate listening sessions and cultural moments designed to give subscribers closer access to artists and music.Spotify says the rewards are curated around how subscribers actually live, travel and shop, positioning the initiative less as a set of discount coupons and more as an extension of the value of being a Premium member.Premium Rewards is available through a dedicated microsite, premiumrewards.byspotify.com, where Premium subscribers can browse available rewards and claim offers directly. Spotify says new perks and experiences will be added to the platform on an ongoing basis, suggesting the current lineup of brand partners and events is a starting point rather than a fixed list.The rewards program is live now and available to all Spotify Premium subscribers in India, with no separate sign-up or additional cost beyond an active Premium subscription.Shipra Srivastava, Head of Marketing at Spotify India, framed the launch as an attempt to extend Premium's value beyond the app itself. She said Premium has always centered on delivering the best audio experience — high quality, uninterrupted listening with offline access — and that Premium Rewards is meant to carry that same feeling into subscribers' everyday lives, the brands they engage with and the experiences they remember. She described the goal as making Premium function more like a membership than a plain subscription, adding that the rewards are being offered as a limited-edition experience for now, making the present moment a particularly good time to be a Premium subscriber in India.
Article Summary: Spotify has rolled out Premium Rewards in India. The initiative gives Premium subscribers access to curated brand offers and invite-only live experiences. The rewards are curated around how subscribers actually live, travel and shop. The move adds a lifestyle and events layer on top of the music streaming service's existing offering of ad-free, offline listening.

Article Title: Government asks Meta to revamp algorithms to curb deepfakes, propaganda: Report
Article Text:
Government calls for closer coordination with Meta

Government calls for closer coordination with Meta

Meta scrutiny rises

The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has asked Meta to revamp its algorithms and submit a compliance roadmap to curb the spread of deepfakes, propaganda and other manipulated or illegal content on its platforms, government sources told ANI. According to the report, the government has asked the company to make specific changes to its algorithms to improve the detection and removal of harmful and manipulated content. It has also directed Meta to strengthen its content moderation systems, respond faster to takedown requests from authorised government agencies and comply with data localisation requirements.The directions were issued after a meeting between Meta's technical team and MeitY officials on Friday - August 7, during which the company explained how its current systems detect and handle harmful content online. However, government officials sought specific algorithmic changes to limit the spread of what they described as propaganda, deepfakes and manipulated media across Meta's platforms, the sources said.The government has also called for closer coordination with Meta to speed up the identification and removal of deepfakes, morphed images and misleading posts. According to the sources quoted in the ANI report, the latest discussions are part of a series of meetings between the government and Meta over the handling of harmful and illegal content on the company's platforms.During the discussions, Meta acknowledged gaps in its existing systems and outlined technical measures it could take to tackle deepfakes and other forms of AI-generated or synthetic content, the sources said. Both sides have agreed to continue the discussions, with another meeting expected next week.The government's scrutiny of Meta has increased in recent days over concerns related to deepfakes, Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM) and other harmful content on its platforms. The social media giant had earlier apologised over errors related to CSAM and deepfake content after concerns were raised by the Indian government.The discussions also come after India tightened its rules for AI-generated and synthetically created content. Earlier this year, the government amended the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules to bring synthetically generated information under a separate regulatory framework and introduce additional due diligence requirements for online intermediaries.The new rules aim to improve accountability for AI-generated and manipulated content, including through identification and labelling requirements.
Article Summary: Government has asked Meta to revamp its algorithms and submit a compliance roadmap to curb the spread of deepfakes, propaganda and other manipulated or illegal content. It has also directed Meta to strengthen its content moderation systems, respond faster to takedown requests from authorised government agencies and comply with data localisation requirements. The government's scrutiny of Meta has increased in recent days.

Article Title: ICE is chasing a 'body camera' August deadline for every officer and agent in the field
Article Text:
ICE may rollout body camera after scrutiny over fatal shootings

The US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) expects to equip every officer and agent working in the field with body cameras by the end of August, marking a major expansion of the agency's use of body-worn cameras during immigration enforcement operations. According to a report by the Associated Press (AP), acting ICE Director David J. Venturella said the agency is "committed to transparency and accountability" and is "on track to equip every officer and agent in the field with body-worn cameras by the end of August."The rollout comes as ICE faces increased scrutiny following two fatal shootings involving its officers in July. In one case, a 25-year-old motorist was fatally shot in Maine by an ICE officer with a history of violent behavior. Days earlier, another ICE officer fatally shot a Houston homebuilder who was driving to work. Neither incident was captured on body camera footage.ICE also defended its policy governing body-worn camera footage after questions were raised about provisions that allow agency leadership to withhold or delay the release of videos involving serious injuries or deaths in custody.According to Venturella, the restrictions are intended to protect investigations and individual privacy and are consistent with federal law as well as policies followed by other federal law enforcement agencies.He also said footage should not be released if doing so could compromise ongoing investigations or privacy.The agency's expanded body camera program is expected to create a much larger visual record of immigration enforcement activities across the United States. However, whether the public will be able to view the footage will continue to depend on ICE's policies governing its release.
Article Summary: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement expects to equip every officer and agent working in the field with body cameras by the end of August. Acting ICE Director David J. Venturella said the agency is "committed to transparency and accountability" The rollout comes as ICE faces increased scrutiny following two fatal shootings involving its officers in July.

Article Title: Government says no UPI charges for users; majority of merchant transactions to remain free
Article Text:
Good news for UPI users: no transaction charges will be applied to UPI payments. Individual transfers between users remain entirely fee-free, while specific merchant transactions above a predetermined threshold may incur a minor Merchant Discount Rate. This legislative change is intended to secure the continuous growth and longevity of UPI, as the government aims to solidify its status as a cutting-edge payment platform.

Here’s what the Ministry of Finance stated in its release

The Ministry of Finance has clarified that UPI users will not have to pay any transaction charges, amid concerns over recent changes proposed under the Payment and Settlement Systems (PSS) Act. In a statement, the ministry said all person-to-person (P2P) UPI transactions will continue to remain free. It also said that even if a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) is introduced in the future, it will apply only to a limited set of merchant transactions above a certain threshold and at a nominal rate. The ministry said the amendment to the PSS Act is meant to support UPI's long-term growth and sustainability, and not to impose charges on ordinary users.“The Government of India wishes to categorically state:No charges for users: Consumers making payments will not face any transaction charges.P2P transactions free: All Person-to-Person transactions will continue to be free of charge.Nominal MDR for merchants: As and when MDR charges are introduced, they will apply only to a limited set of merchant transactions, above a certain threshold, at a nominal rate, far lower than debit or credit card MDRs.Vast majority of the transactions will remain free of charge for merchants on UPI. MDR, if introduced, will only be threshold based and not blanketly levied to all.Once the Parliament passes the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which proposes to amend Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, the “UPI and Services Steering Committee” headed by NPCI will decide on the MDR, if any.Why amend the Payment and Settlement Systems ActIn an official release, the government stated that the amendment is an enabling provision designed to ensure UPI’s long-term sustainability, technological advancement, and resilience against emerging risks.Growth of UPI: With exponential transaction volumes, the system requires significant and continuous upgrades in cybersecurity, fraud prevention, and infrastructure.Market Expansion: It is necessary to increase competition by encouraging more companies to expand their operations, which requires a self-sustaining revenue model.Self-sustainability: Reliance on subsidies alone is not viable for the next wave of growth. A balanced framework is required to ensure that UPI remains robust, inclusive, and future-ready.Continuing further, the ministry stated:India now stands at the cusp of the next wave of digital payments growth. To expand UPI further into rural and semi-urban areas and maintain competitiveness, the UPI ecosystem must be self- sustainable and affordable. The amendment to the PSS Act is a forward-looking step to ensure that UPI continues to thrive as a secure, affordable, inclusive, and globally recognized payment system.
Article Summary: The Ministry of Finance has clarified that UPI users will not have to pay any transaction charges. This comes amid concerns over recent changes proposed under the Payment and Settlement Systems (PSS) Act. In a statement, the ministry said all person-to-person (P2P) UPI transactions will continue to remain free.

Article Title: ICICI Bank warn customers; says scammers target people looking for quick loans
Article Text:
ICICI Bank tells how to safeguard your self from loan scams

Reporting suspicious activity

ICICI Bank has issued an advisory warning for its customers about the increasing cases of instant load fraud. Scammers often lure people seeking quick loads by promising instant approval with minimal checks. The bank stated that fraudsters create fake loan apps and websites which appear to be legitimate and then approach victims via phone calls, SMS, instant chat messages, or social media. They typically demand sensitive personal information such as Aadhaar numbers, bank details or passwords. In many cases the scammers also insist on an advance fee or security deposit for loan disbursal, pressurising victims to act quickly with claims of time-bound offers. Once the payment is made, they disappear.In a mail sent to its customers, ICICI bank advise the customers to be cautious of unsolicited loan offers received via calls, emails, or advertisements. If an offer seems “too good to be true” with little paperwork or no credit checks, it is likely a scam. Genuine lenders never ask for upfront payments before disbursing loans. Customers are urged to never share personal or financial details such as date of birth, OTPs, passwords, CVV numbers, or bank account information.•Unsolicited Offers: Be cautious of loan offers you receive unexpectedly via calls, e-mails or advertisements•Too Good to Be True: If the loan offer seems unusually easy with little paperwork or no credit checks, it’s likely a scam•Advance Fees: Genuine lenders never ask for upfront payments before disbursing a loan•Never share personal or financial details like DOB, OTPs,passwords, CVV numbers or bank detailsIf you receive a suspicious loan offer, disconnect immediately and report it through official channels.•Report online fraud on the National Cyber Crime portal at cybercrime.gov.in, call the helpline number 1930 or call ICICI Bank helpline on 1800 2662•If you have received any malicious / phishing / suspicious e-mails or calls, please report these to Sanchar Saathi at sancharsaathi.gov.in and to ICICI Bank at antiphishing@icici.bank.in
Article Summary: ICICI Bank has issued an advisory warning for its customers about the increasing cases of instant load fraud. Scammers often lure people seeking quick loads by promising instant approval with minimal checks. The bank stated that fraudsters create fake loan apps and websites which appear to be legitimate.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Jensen Huang: “The world can be unfair and deal you with tough cards. Swiftly shake it off…”; a reminder to keep moving forward
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Jensen Huang

“The world can be unfair and deal you with tough cards. Swiftly shake it off. There’s another opportunity out there — or create one.”

What does today’s quote mean

What does 'tough cards' really mean

‘Shake it off’ is about moving forward, not pretending

Why creating an opportunity is harder than finding one

All about the Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang

Huang’s career offers a practical example of changing direction

Why Huang’s advice matters in a changing job market

There is a difference between accepting reality and giving up

Lessons learnt from Jensen Huang’s quote

Not every setback is within your control. A poor outcome does not always reflect a lack of ability, effort or preparation.

Accept what has happened, then move forward. Dwelling on an outcome that cannot be changed can prevent attention from shifting towards what is still possible.

Do not confuse persistence with repeating the same mistake. Staying committed to a goal can sometimes mean changing the route rather than continuing with an approach that is no longer working.

Look beyond the opportunity you originally wanted. A lost job, failed idea or missed promotion may force you to consider possibilities that were not part of the original plan.

Create opportunities when none are obvious. Building a new skill, starting a project or finding another use for existing experience can open a route that did not previously exist.

Learn from failure without romanticising it. Not every setback has a hidden benefit, but most can provide information that helps shape the next decision.

Separate circumstances from self-worth. A rejection or failure is an event, not necessarily a judgement on a person's overall ability or potential.

Adapt when the circumstances change. Careers, industries and technologies evolve, and being willing to adjust can be more useful than holding tightly to an outdated plan.

Setbacks rarely arrive at convenient moments. A job application can fail after weeks of preparation, a business idea can lose momentum just when it appears ready to grow, a promotion can go to someone else, or a carefully made plan can become impossible because circumstances change. Some disappointments are the result of poor decisions; others have little to do with merit at all. That is part of what makes setbacks difficult to process. There is not always a lesson neatly waiting inside them, but sometimes things simply go wrong. Jensen Huang, the co-founder and chief executive of Nvidia, has offered a straightforward way of looking at such moments: accept that the hand may be bad, then decide what can be done with whatever comes next.Huang’s words begin with a simple truth: life can be unfair. People can work hard and still face setbacks because of circumstances beyond their control. A disappointing result does not always reflect their ability.But he does not suggest dwelling on what went wrong. Instead, he encourages people to shake it off, move ahead and search for another chance.If there is no opportunity waiting, the answer may be to create one yourself.Huang's reference to cards is a familiar metaphor for circumstances outside a person's control. In a card game, a player can make sensible decisions and still receive a poor hand. Skill matters, but it does not determine every starting condition.The same is true outside a game. Someone can prepare carefully for an interview and still lose the position. A company can develop a product responsibly and discover that customers do not want it. A talented employee can find themselves in a shrinking industry. A business can be affected by an economic shock that has nothing to do with the quality of its work.The metaphor is useful precisely because it leaves room for unfairness. There is no suggestion that every difficult result is deserved or that every failure contains some hidden benefit. Huang's point begins with acknowledging that people do not control all the circumstances in which they operate.The phrase “shake it off” can sound dismissive when taken on its own. A serious setback cannot always be brushed aside in an afternoon.In the context of the full quote, however, it is less about denying disappointment and more about refusing to remain stuck inside it.That distinction matters. Accepting that something went wrong is not the same as deciding that it did not matter. A person can be disappointed, angry or frustrated and still recognise that the result cannot be changed.The useful question then becomes a practical one: what remains possible?Huang's wording suggests that the answer should be sought relatively quickly. The past outcome may deserve reflection, particularly if there is something to learn from it, but reflection can eventually become repetition. There is a point at which analysing the lost opportunity no longer changes what happens next.There is a comfortable assumption that opportunities are things that already exist and that successful people are simply better at spotting them.Huang's wording challenges that assumption. An opportunity can sometimes emerge from an activity that initially looks too small or uncertain to matter. A side project can become professional experience. A technical experiment can reveal a new application. A failed product can expose a different customer need. A conversation can lead to work that was never formally advertised. Creating an opportunity does not mean manufacturing success from nothing. Resources, timing and circumstances still matter.It means recognising that the next useful possibility may not arrive in the form you were expecting. That is a subtler message than “never give up”. It allows for changing the goal itself.Huang was born in Taiwan in 1963 and moved to the United States as a child. He studied electrical engineering at Oregon State University before earning a master's degree in electrical engineering from Stanford University. Before founding Nvidia, he worked at LSI Logic and Advanced Micro Devices.In 1993, Huang co-founded Nvidia with Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem. He has remained the company's president and chief executive, guiding it through several major shifts in computing.Nvidia initially became known for graphics processors, particularly as computer graphics and gaming developed. The company's GPU technology later found a much wider role in scientific computing, machine learning and artificial intelligence.That history is relevant because Nvidia's eventual importance in AI was not the company's original story. Its technology became useful for workloads far beyond the graphics applications that first made GPUs widely recognised.The development of Nvidia provides an unusually clear example of why the second half of Huang's quote matters.Graphics remained important, but GPUs turned out to be well suited to highly parallel calculations. That opened opportunities in areas that were not necessarily the obvious destination when the technology was first developed.The company invested in CUDA, a software platform that allowed developers to use GPUs for general-purpose computing. Over time, that helped create an ecosystem around accelerated computing and made Nvidia hardware increasingly useful for researchers and developers working with machine learning.The significance of this history is not that every unsuccessful experiment eventually becomes a breakthrough. That would be too neat a reading. It is that technology can acquire value in ways that are difficult to predict at the beginning.A company can build capabilities for one purpose and later discover that those capabilities solve a different problem particularly well.The idea has particular relevance to careers because professional paths are rarely as linear as they once appeared.Industries change. Companies restructure. Technologies replace some tasks while creating others. Skills that were valuable five years ago can become less sought after, while entirely new specialisms can emerge quickly.Artificial intelligence has made that shift particularly visible. Workers are having to reconsider which skills are durable, which tasks can be automated and where human judgement remains valuable. In that environment, Huang's advice can be read less as a motivational slogan and more as a practical approach to uncertainty.A person may not be able to control how quickly an industry changes. They may not be able to prevent a company from cutting jobs. What they can sometimes control is whether they develop another capability before the need becomes urgent. That is the “create one” part of the quote in a modern setting.Huang's advice should not be confused with passive acceptance. Accepting that something has gone wrong is often the first step towards making a sensible decision. Giving up is different. It means deciding that no useful alternative exists. The quote leaves room between those two positions. A person can accept that a particular opportunity has disappeared while continuing to look for another. They can admit that a business plan failed without deciding that entrepreneurship itself is impossible. They can recognise that a career path has changed without concluding that their professional life has reached a dead end.

Article Title: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani extends tax deadline after residents complain that emails you warned us about are 'unclear'

Zohran Mamdani

Background of pied-à-terre tax introduced by Zohran Mamdani

When Jeff Bezos reminded Zohran Mamdani: Taxes on 5-star hotels are popular

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced that the deadline for homeowners to submit exemptions applications for the city’s new pied-à-terre tax has been extended to September 18, four weeks beyond original August 21 cutoff, according to a report by Business Insider. Kathy Hochul, the measure is expected to generate about $500 million annually to help close the city’s $2.2 billion budget shortfall. The tax has angered wealthy residents including Ken Griffin and Bill Ackman, while President Donald Trump criticized Mamdani in April for “destroying” New York City.In related news, Amazon founder Jeff Bezos recently weighed in on New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s proposed pied-à-terre tax, which would levy an annual surcharge on non-primary residences valued at $5 million or more, according to a report by Fortune. Bezos, who himself owns a residence in the city, said that the proposed tax itself was ‘a fine thing for New York to do’, likening it to hotels that fall on out-of-towners. Bezos has cautioned that increasing the hotel taxes too aggressively could backfire. “If you raise the hotel taxes too much, tourists stop coming. So you have to be judicious,” he said, urging city leaders to balance revenue generation with economic competitiveness.Bezos also criticised Mamdani’s April 14 video filmed outside Citadel CEO Ken Griffin’s Central Park South penthouse, which announced the tax proposal. “Ken Griffin isn’t a villain. He hasn’t hurt anybody. He’s not hurting New York. In fact, quite the opposite,” Bezos said, rejecting what he called the “villain strategy” of targeting individuals. Griffin had called the video “creepy” and threatened to cancel a $6 billion Midtown development project, prompting mediation by Governor Kathy Hochul.
Article Summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced that the deadline for homeowners to submit exemptions applications for the city’s new pied-à-terre tax has been extended to September 18. The move comes after residents complained that the notification e-mails were unclear and the exemption process overly complicated.

Article Title: In 1997, after returning to Apple, 11 years after he was fired from the company he founded, Steve Jobs at staff townhall: Nike sells shoes, and yet …
Article Text:
Steve Jobs reportedly wanted Apple to sell an idea, not specifications

Steve Jobs praised Nike's marketing strategy

Steve Jobs wanted Apple to sell an idea, not specifications

When Steve Jobs returned to Apple in 1997, 11 years after he was forced out of the company he co-founded, one of his first priorities was not just fixing Apple's products but rebuilding its brand. During a staff town hall then, Steve Jobs pointed to Nike as what he called one of the world's best marketing examples. Although Nike "sells shoes," he said people associate the company with something much bigger than its products. Jobs also used that example to explain why Apple should stop focusing only on technical specifications and instead tell customers what the company stands for. His thinking later shaped Apple's iconic "Think Different" campaign.Addressing Apple employees, Jobs said the company's brand had weakened during the years he was away and needed to be rebuilt. "The Apple brand has clearly suffered from neglect," Jobs said. "We need to bring it back."He then highlighted Nike as an example of strong branding. "The best example of all, and one of the greatest jobs of marketing the universe has ever seen is Nike," Jobs said. "Remember, Nike sells a commodity. They sell shoes. And yet when you think of Nike, you feel something different than a shoe company."According to Jobs, Nike's advertisements were successful because they focused on athletes and inspiration instead of product features."In their ads, they don't ever talk about their products. They don't ever tell you about their air soles and why they're better than Reebok's air soles. What does Nike do? They honor great athletes and they honor great athletics. That's who they are, that's what they are about," he said.Steve Jobs said Apple needed to follow a similar approach instead of talking about processor speeds or comparing itself with competitors. "The way to do that is not to talk about speeds and feeds. It's not to talk about MIPS and megahertz, it's not to talk about why we're better than Windows," he said.That philosophy led to Apple's famous "Think Different" campaign, which featured personalities such as Albert Einstein, Martin Luther King Jr. and John Lennon. Rather than highlighting computer specifications, the campaign focused on creativity, innovation and Apple's larger mission.
Article Summary: Steve Jobs praised Nike's marketing strategy during a staff town hall. He said people associate the company with something much bigger than its products. Jobs said Apple should stop focusing only on technical specifications and instead tell customers what the company stands for. His thinking later shaped Apple's iconic "Think Different" campaign.

Article Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's joke on parenting that created a heated debate over Asian parenting

How the joke by Jensen Hunag sparked debate

A joke and candid conversation by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang about growing up with strict Asian parents has snowballed into a much larger public conversation about parenting styles, criticism, and how children process being pushed to their limits. During a recent conversation at a public event, Huang joked, “Once you’ve been raised by Asian parents, you need therapy for life.” He then explained that how his parents were ‘classic Asian parents’ who constantly pushed him to improve, rarely offering praise but always pointed out what could be better. Huang further added that his strict upbringing taught him humility and resilience, and also helped him to accept criticism and stay focused on improvement even as he leads one of the world’s most valuable tech companies.Huang further shared that his father continues to give him suggestions event at the age of 63, underscoring how deeply ingrained this style of parenting is. He also stressed on the fact that he never saw criticism as discouragement, but rather as a form of love and belief in his potential. He added that for him, the relentless feedback became a foundation for his ability to handle pressure and thrive in competitive environments.Huang framed this upbringing generously rather than bitterly. He said his parents' way of showing love was to criticize, and that being raised that way left him with no trouble taking criticism, no trouble learning new things, and no trouble staying humble. He extended the logic into his leadership philosophy at Nvidia, saying that if he genuinely cares about someone, he owes them thoughtful, detailed criticism rather than an easy "good job. "What initially started as a self-deprecating aside at an industry event has since been widely shared and started a heated debate online majorly across the Asian and Asian-American spaces. According to report a China Daily, Nvidia CEO made the remarks just day ahead of China's college entrance exam, the gaokao, which offered added resonance and triggered a wider debate over Asian, and specifically Chinese, parenting norms.Supporters of Huang's framing point to his own trajectory as evidence the approach works: a childhood shaped by relentless correction that, in his telling, forged the resilience, humility and appetite for learning that helped build one of the most valuable companies in the world. On the other hand, the critics of this point of view said that the ‘never good enough’ model of parenting, even when well-intentioned, can leave lasting emotional costs that success doesn't erase, arguing that Huang's own joke, that this kind of upbringing requires a lifetime of therapy, undercuts the case for holding it up as an ideal.

Article Title: 'Turned it in…': Google's 30th employee Jeff Dean posts photo of everything he handed back on his last day at Google after 27 years
Article Text:
The stickers on Jeff Dean's laptop are a working history of Google AI

What Jeff Dean's farewell email to Google employees actually said

Jeff Dean's final act as a Google employee was a photograph. On Friday, the man who joined the company as employee number 30 in 1999 posted a picture of the two things he surrendered on his way out the door: a scuffed black Google laptop, and the plastic-sleeved badge with his face on it, still marked FTE. The caption ran to three words.The post has since crossed 2.8 million views, which tells you something about how closely the industry has been watching this particular exit. It comes days after Google announced a sweeping AI leadership reshuffle that moved Demis Hassabis out of the Google DeepMind CEO role and into a chair position, with CTO Koray Kavukcuoglu stepping up as SVP. Dean is leaving alongside Sanjay Ghemawat, Oriol Vinyals and Quoc Le to co-found Discovery Loop, a public benefit corporation backed by Alphabet, Radical Ventures and Khosla Ventures.The laptop is the better artefact, and it appears to be a Chromebook, a modest daily driver for the man who built Google's AI infrastructure. Its lid carries a rainbow-sliced anatomical brain, the old Google Brain logo, a TensorFlow decal, a sticker from something called the Optic Nerve 2020 Summit, a tiny Android figure, and a hand-drawn cartoon of a very large table with the words "BIG TABLE" scrawled underneath.Dean co-created BigTable. He co-authored TensorFlow. He founded Google Brain in 2011.Nearly every sticker on that lid is a thing he built, which is either charming or slightly unhinged depending on your view of engineer merch.When one user asked whether he had really kept the same machine for six years, Dean replied that he thought so, maybe five. Google's chief scientist, apparently, does not chase hardware refresh cycles.Dean also shared the internal note he sent colleagues, and it reads less like a resignation than an inventory. He listed growing Search's index 100 times over and its query rate 1,000 times. Building the first Google Ads system. Launching Google News and Translate. MapReduce, Spanner, DistBelief, Pathways. Starting the TPU programme. Kicking off Gemini with Vinyals as co-tech-lead.Then the smaller stuff, which is the part people are actually sharing: biking to offsites in Monterey, the "Run or Else…" group runs, changing desks 18 times, and visiting 29 Google offices across five continents. He noted that a Google badge could get you a cappuccino in more than 100 cities. That badge is now in a photograph.Dean will be CEO at Discovery Loop, which plans to automate the experimental loop itself, running thousands of AI-designed experiments in parallel across machine learning, chip design and drug discovery. Sundar Pichai called it a privilege to have worked alongside Dean and Ghemawat, and Alphabet is providing compute for the first year.Inside Google, employees reacted mostly with memes. One line summed up the mood well: Google isn't losing Jeff Dean, it's open-sourcing him.
Article Summary: Jeff Dean is leaving Google to co-found Discovery Loop. He joined the company as employee number 30 in 1999. Dean shared a picture of his laptop and badge on his way out the door. The post has since crossed 2.8 million views.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Sam Altman: “Focus on adding another zero to…” - a powerful lesson on ambition and success
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Sam Altman

“Focus on adding another zero to whatever you define as your success metric.”

Understanding the meaning of the quote

The difference between gradual growth and a change in scale

The metric itself needs careful thought

Why the idea is not simply about ambition

The quote can apply outside business

The danger of choosing the wrong metric

How the idea can be used in practical terms

The deeper idea behind the extra zero

Success is often discussed as though it has a fixed meaning. For some people, it is money. For others, it may be the number of people reached, businesses built, problems solved or work completed to a certain standard. The measure changes from person to person, but the way that measure is approached can change the outcome just as much. Sam Altman has written about this in the context of careers, ambition and leverage, arguing that people should think beyond incremental gains. His advice can be summed up in one line: “Focus on adding another zero to whatever you define as your success metric.” The idea sounds simple, but it points towards a different way of thinking about progress and scale.The phrase “adding another zero” is essentially about changing the scale of the goal rather than simply working harder towards the same result. If a person defines success as reaching 10, the idea is to consider what it would take to reach 100. The important part is not the number itself, but the change in thinking that comes with a much larger target.A goal that is ten times bigger can expose the limits of an existing approach. Reaching 10 might require more effort, while reaching 100 could require a new system, technology, team, business model or way of distributing the work. The question changes from how to do slightly more to what would need to be different altogether.Altman also leaves the definition of success open. The metric does not necessarily have to be money. It could be revenue, customers, readers, users, influence, discoveries or any other result that matters to a person. The first step is deciding what success actually means. The next is asking what would need to change to make that result ten times larger.A person can improve their skills, become more efficient and gradually earn more over several years. That kind of growth can be useful and, in many careers, necessary. But Altman’s argument is aimed at something different: opportunities where the relationship between effort and outcome can change.A small improvement often comes from doing the same thing slightly better. A much larger improvement may require doing something else.That distinction is easy to overlook because incremental progress is visible. A new qualification, another client or a modest salary increase can be measured immediately. A change in direction is harder to evaluate because its outcome may not be clear for some time.Yet the larger opportunities can sometimes sit outside the existing routine.There is a detail in Altman’s wording that matters. He does not say to add another zero to income, wealth or company valuation. He says to add another zero to “whatever you define as your success metric”. That makes the idea broader.For a writer, success might be the number of readers who find the work useful rather than the number of articles produced. For a business, it might be customers or revenue. A scientist could define it through discoveries or applications of research. A teacher might care about the number of students who develop a lasting interest in a subject. The choice of metric influences behaviour.If a person measures success purely by the number of tasks completed, they may become focused on speed. If they measure success by the quality of outcomes, they may make different decisions about where to spend their time.“Add another zero” could easily be read as an instruction to chase bigger numbers indefinitely. That would miss an important part of the idea. A tenfold target is useful because it can challenge the assumptions behind the current method. It is not useful merely because the number is larger. There are situations where increasing scale is undesirable. A business might prioritise quality over volume. A writer may prefer a smaller audience that is genuinely engaged. A company may decide that rapid expansion would damage the product or its culture. The metric therefore has to be chosen carefully. Altman’s wording gives people room to define success for themselves rather than prescribing a single version of it.Altman is closely associated with startups and artificial intelligence, but the underlying idea is not restricted to entrepreneurs. A journalist might ask how to reach ten times as many readers without simply producing ten times as many articles. That could lead to better distribution, stronger reporting, a recognisable editorial voice or a different publishing model.An educator could ask how to help ten times as many students without teaching ten times the number of classes. Online material, training systems and collaboration could change the scale.An independent creator might think about how one piece of work can continue reaching people rather than disappearing once it has been published.In each case, the extra zero changes the question. The focus moves away from personal effort alone and towards systems that can extend the impact of that effort.There is a less obvious problem with the idea of multiplying a metric. Not everything important is easy to measure. A business may be able to track revenue, users and sales with precision, but customer trust is harder to reduce to a single number. A publication can count page views, yet those figures do not necessarily reveal whether readers found the journalism useful.When a measurable target becomes the main objective, people can sometimes begin optimising for the number rather than the thing the number was meant to represent. That makes the first part of Altman’s quote just as important as the second. Before adding the zero, the metric needs to make sense.One way to apply the concept is to take an existing goal and multiply it by ten. Then ask what would have to change.If the answer is simply “I need to work ten times harder”, the current system may not contain enough leverage. If the answer involves automation, delegation, technology, a different audience, a new product or a different business model, the exercise has done something useful. It has exposed the limits of the existing approach. The goal does not necessarily need to be achieved immediately. In some cases, the value lies in understanding why the current system cannot support it and identifying what could make a larger outcome possible.That is a more practical interpretation than treating the quote as a command to constantly pursue bigger numbers.At its core, the quote is about the relationship between goals and methods. A person who wants a small improvement can often make small adjustments. A person who wants a result ten times larger may have to reconsider the entire way the work is being done. That is why the extra zero matters.It changes the scale of the question enough to expose what the existing system can and cannot do. It can reveal where leverage is missing, whether the chosen metric is useful and whether an opportunity has enough potential to justify the effort being invested in it.Sam Altman’s line is therefore less about the number itself than about what happens when the number becomes large enough to make the old assumptions uncomfortable. The zero is only the visible part.
Article Summary: Sam Altman says people should think beyond incremental gains. His advice can be summed up in one line: ‘Focus on adding another zero to whatever you define as your success metric’ The idea sounds simple, but it points towards a different way of thinking about progress and scale.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Reid Hoffman, ‘The world is constantly changing & we are constantly changing. Your identity isn't found through introspection but rather emerges through experimentation’
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Reid Hoffman

The meaning behind the words

The Startup of You

Why introspection alone falls short

Identity as an ongoing experiment

The broader lesson

Reid Hoffman has spent his career moving between reinvention and risk — from co-founding LinkedIn and helping shape the early trajectory of PayPal, to becoming one of Silicon Valley's most sought-after venture capitalists at Greylock, to more recently helping steer the direction of AI through his role on OpenAI's early board and his involvement with companies like Microsoft and the Arc Institute. Few people in tech have shifted roles, industries and identities as often, or as visibly, as he has. When Hoffman writes about identity not being something you find but something you build through action, he is describing a principle his own career has repeatedly tested.“The world is constantly changing & we are constantly changing, your identity isn't found through introspection but rather emerges through experimentation.”Reid Hoffman co-founded LinkedIn, sits on the boards of Microsoft and the Arc Institute, and has spent decades as one of Silicon Valley's most influential venture capitalists at Greylock. The quote comes from his book, co-authored with Ben Casnocha, which applies startup thinking to individual careers. Hoffman's central argument in the book is that people should treat their own lives less like a fixed plan to be followed and more like an early-stage company: something built through iteration, testing and adjustment rather than a single moment of self-discovery.This particular quote pushes back against a deeply embedded cultural belief — that somewhere inside each person is a "true self" waiting to be uncovered through quiet reflection. Hoffman argues the opposite. Identity, in his view, isn't a fixed object hidden beneath the surface, waiting for enough introspection to reveal it. It's something that takes shape gradually, through actions taken and experiences lived, and it keeps shifting because both the world and the person navigating it keep changing.Reflection has real value — it helps people process experience and notice patterns in what they enjoy or avoid. But Hoffman's point is that reflection without action has limits. A person can spend years thinking about what they might be good at or what might make them happy, and arrive at very different conclusions than they would after simply trying the thing.This is because aspirations aren't as stable as they feel. What someone wants shapes what they do, but the reverse is also true — what someone does reshapes what they want. A person who tries a new role, a new city, a new creative pursuit, or a new way of working often discovers preferences and strengths that pure thinking would never have surfaced, simply because those preferences didn't exist yet in any meaningful form until they were tested against reality.Hoffman's framing treats identity less like a noun and more like a verb — something continuously in motion. Since the world itself doesn't hold still, the version of "who you are" that made sense five years ago may not fit the circumstances, tools, relationships or opportunities available today. Clinging to an old, fixed self-concept in a changed environment can become as limiting as never having a sense of identity at all.This is not a call for aimlessness. Hoffman isn't suggesting people abandon direction or planning. Rather, he's suggesting that plans should be treated as hypotheses — informed guesses worth testing, revising, and sometimes discarding, rather than fixed identities to defend. In his broader work on entrepreneurship, this mirrors exactly how he advises founders to treat a business: not as a single idea to be protected at all costs, but as a series of experiments refined by real feedback from the world.Hoffman's quote reframes a source of anxiety many people carry — the pressure to "figure out who they are" — as a misunderstanding of how identity actually works. There's no fixed answer sitting in wait, only a process of engaging with the world, learning from what happens, and adjusting accordingly. In that sense, not having it all figured out isn't a failure of self-awareness. It's simply what it looks like to be in the middle of becoming someone.
Article Summary: Reid Hoffman co-founded LinkedIn, sits on the boards of Microsoft and the Arc Institute. The quote comes from his book, co-authored with Ben Casnocha, which applies startup thinking to individual careers. Hoffman's framing treats identity less like a noun and more like a verb — something continuously in motion.

Article Title: After Hugging Face hack, OpenAI pauses work on Astra AI model over cybersecurity risks
Article Text:
OpenAI's first ChatGPT-powered device is said to be a smart speaker

OpenAI’s internal evaluations of Astra

OpenAI models accessed the internet and hacked Hugging Face

ChatGPT-maker OpenAI has announced that it is pausing some activities involving its upcoming artificial intelligence model Astra, after internal evaluations concluded the company ‘cannot rule out critical cyber capabilities. ’ The company revealed the decision in a detailed blog post, marks one of the first times an AI developer has publicly slowed model development due to security risks. “We believe advanced cyber-capable models should help defenders identify and address vulnerabilities before attackers do. We’re committed to working alongside governments, safety institutes, and civil society to ensure that the frontier capabilities of models like Astra, and those that follow, are deployed responsibly and broadly for the benefit of all humanity,” the company said in a blog post.OpenAI revealed that during the recent evaluations, Asrta demonstrated advanced coding and cybersecurity abilities that pushed it closer to the ‘critical’ threshold outlined in OpenAI’s Preparedness Framework. First introduced in 2023, the framework requires researchers to halt further development if a model can autonomously exploit vulnerabilities or carry out end-to-end cyberattacks against hardened targets.OpenAI said it is continuing to benchmark Astra but has paused internal work that does not meet heightened security requirements.The move follows a series of incidents across the AI industry where models escaped testing environments. In July, two OpenAI models accessed the internet and hacked open-source provider Hugging Face. Anthropic later disclosed its models had hacked three companies during testing, while Meta and Chinese startup Moonshot AI also reported breaches of testing constraints. These events have fueled concerns about companies’ ability to control increasingly capable AI systems.Jeffrey Ladish, executive director of Palisade Research, said OpenAI should have paused Astra earlier, following the Hugging Face incident. “It’s definitely late. We are clearly at the point where… we should be losing a lot of trust in AI companies to actually self-regulate,” he told the Wall Street Journal. OpenAI clarified that Astra was not involved in the Hugging Face exploit but did not provide a release timeline for the model.OpenAI said it is implementing universal monitoring and tighter testing environments for Astra, while partnering with government agencies and third-party auditors to expand safety evaluations. After the Hugging Face hack, the company worked with CrowdStrike, METR, and Redwood Research to conduct independent assessments.
Article Summary: OpenAI’s internal evaluations of Astra demonstrated advanced coding and cybersecurity abilities that pushed it closer to the ‘critical’ threshold outlined in the Preparedness Framework. In July, two OpenAI models accessed the internet and hacked open-source provider Hugging Face. OpenAI said it is implementing universal monitoring and tighter testing environments for Astra.

Article Title: Under US government's new proposed rule, H-1B visa workers would be required to leave US immediately and cannot change their status or employers unless USCIS ...
Article Text:
The proposed H-1B visa rule is currently under review

What the proposed H-1B visa rule could change

Who is covered by the current grace period

What happens next

A proposed rule by the US government could remove the 60-day grace period currently available to H-1B visa holders and several other temporary workers after they lose their jobs. If the proposal is approved, affected workers may have to leave the United States immediately and would generally not be able to change their immigration status or switch employers from within the country unless the US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) decides to forgive the lapse in status. According to a Bloomberg report, the proposal is currently under review.The proposal is currently being reviewed by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB). Once the review is complete, it will be published in the Federal Register for a public comment period of 30 to 60 days before any final decision is made.If the rule is finalized, foreign workers whose employment ends before their visa period expires would generally no longer be considered to be maintaining lawful status. As a result, they would be required to leave the US immediately and would not be allowed to change employers or switch to another visa category while remaining in the country, unless USCIS exercises its discretion to excuse the lapse in status.The current 60-day grace period was introduced in 2016 and took effect in early 2017. It applies to several categories of temporary workers, including those on H-1B, H-1B1, L-1, O-1, TN, E-1, E-2 and E-3 visas, along with their eligible dependents.Under the existing rule, workers who lose their jobs can remain in the US for up to 60 days, or until their I-94 expires, whichever comes first. During this period, they can look for a new employer, apply for a change of visa status, or prepare to leave the country. The grace period applies whether a worker resigns or is laid off.The proposal is still under federal review and has not been published in full. Once it is released, the public will be able to submit comments before the government decides whether to finalize the rule.Immigration attorneys and employers are likely to watch the proposal closely because any change to post-employment rules could affect workforce planning, hiring timelines and relocation decisions for companies that rely on skilled foreign professionals across multiple industries.If adopted, the regulation would mark a major change for H-1B workers and other temporary visa holders by removing the current buffer period that allows them to remain in the US after losing their jobs while exploring other immigration or employment options.
Article Summary: The proposal is currently under review by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Once the review is complete, it will be published in the Federal Register for a public comment period of 30 to 60 days before any final decision is made. If the rule is finalized, foreign workers whose employment ends before their visa period expires would generally no longer be considered to be maintaining lawful status. They would be required to leave the US immediately.

Article Title: Godfather of AI Geoffrey Hinton on OpenAI, Meta and Anthropic AI models hacking other companies: What is happening is ...
Article Text:
‘Godfather of AI’ Geoffrey Hinton on AI agents hacking other companies

Frontier models escape testing environments

Challenging corporate reassurances

Geoffrey Hinton, who is widely recognised as the “godfather of AI”, has issued a fresh warning regarding artificial intelligence (AI), stating that as frontier models grow increasingly intelligent, keeping them under human control will become nearly impossible. The Nobel Prize-winning computer scientist highlighted recent cybersecurity incidents where AI agents from companies like Anthropic and OpenAI escaped isolated testing environments and hacked other companies, calling the developments "somewhat scary."“What’s happening is these things are getting smarter," Hinton said at the Ai4 artificial intelligence conference in Las Vegas Click, adding, “I think as they get smarter, we’re going to see more and more complex intentions they have – and more and more ability to escape control."Hinton’s comments follow public disclosures from leading AI laboratories regarding autonomous security breaches. Over the past month, OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta Platforms revealed that several of their frontier AI models managed to breach digital “sandboxes”, which are isolated testing networks built to contain unreleased AI, and gain unauthorised access to external systems.Adding to those concerns, the UK AI Security Institute (AISI) recently reported that Anthropic’s advanced Mythos model created false online personas, contacted real individuals without prompting and attempted to deploy malicious code updates to an open-source project.Hinton warned that these incidents signal the beginning of a wave of AI-driven cyber threats.“I anticipate there will be lots of nasty cyberattacks. The problem is the attacker only needs to be successful once, and the defender needs to be successful every time,” Hinton said during a panel discussion.Hinton rejected claims from major technology corporations that advanced AI models can be easily governed or kept safe through standard software constraints, arguing that reliance on outsmarting super-intelligent software is fundamentally flawed once models surpass human cognitive abilities across multiple domains.He also cautioned the public to remain critical of safety promises issued by technology firms heavily invested in AI development.“Companies investing in AI have a vested interest in telling you two things: One, it won’t go rogue. And two, it won’t cause mass unemployment,” Hinton stated, reiterating his view that there remains a 10% to 20% probability that unchecked AI could pose an existential risk to humanity.
Article Summary: ‘Godfather of AI’ Geoffrey Hinton on AI agents hacking other companies. Frontier models escape testing environments and hack other companies, Hinton says. Hinton: As frontier models grow increasingly intelligent, keeping them under human control will become nearly impossible.
